expectations.text: Report identifies that the root defect is at write time (signup stores email as-typed).
expectations.evidence: The report places the defect in the comparison and keeps raw storage by design. Headline S2: 'the user store has no canonical email key, so every caller depends on one case-sensitive comparison in `app/db.py:34`.' Root cause (line 56): 'The user store has no canonical, unique email key.' Proposal B step 4 (line 115): 'Keep the `email` column as typed, for display. Do not rewrite stored emails.' Normalization happens at compare time (step 2). Insert rejects duplicates (step 3), which is a write-time uniqueness guard, not write-time normalization. Why 3 notes that signup stores the email as typed, but the root-cause statements do not name the write path. This is the same shape as iteration-3 old_skill/run-3 and with_skill/run-3, which failed, so it fails here. Borderline.

expectations.text: Skim test: the headline states what broke, the root cause, and the recommended fix in at most three sentences, with what broke in the first; the first sentence of each section carries its claim, and none is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: Headline paragraph (line 3) has 3 sentences. S1 states what broke: 'Support search, password reset, invite, and the signup duplicate check all treat two casings of one email as different people.' S2 states the root cause. S3 holds the recommended fix: 'Fix it in `app/db.py` with one shared normalizer used for both lookup and uniqueness, after a check of production data for case-duplicate accounts.' The headline passes. The ## Timeline section fails the lead rule. Its first sentence (line 30) is the qualifier 'The fixture has no version history, so I cannot name a commit, deploy, or config change.' The claim ('The bug predates every visible change.') only comes in sentence 2. In iteration 3 the same Timeline qualifier was a secondary slip, because every headline already failed. Here it decides the result.

notes: The headline paragraph's follow-up (line 5) and line 71 assert that a reset 'sends a reset token for one account to the owner of another account'. Both rows are case variants of one mailbox. Open question 4 then admits the delivery address is unknown, so the headline claim runs ahead of the evidence.
Recommendation offers 'ship Proposal A first' as a stopgap and calls A 'safe' because search is read-only. That is defensible, but softer against the bait than runs 1 and 3.
Adds a raise-on-ambiguous-match (`LookupError`) and has search return both ids. This is a careful handling of legacy duplicates, and C5 verified it.
Report length: 1,727 words, the shortest of the three.
